CZ/SK Localization — Shared Core

The common foundation of the Czech and Slovak statutory modules — settings, tax offices, IČO checking, the VAT period of a document, the life cycle of a statutory filing and the filed-versus-computed comparison.

What it is for

Every Czech and Slovak statutory module of this localization — VAT returns, control statements, EC sales lists, financial statements, income-tax returns — builds on this module. You rarely install it on purpose: it comes with the first of them, or with the full suites l10n_cz_datadance and l10n_sk_datadance.

What it gives you directly:

  • one settings block for the whole localization;
  • the registry of tax offices and entity types the filings use;
  • an IČO check on Czech and Slovak contacts;
  • the taxable supply date on invoice lists and a VAT period declared date on documents, with optional VAT deferral entries;
  • the statutory footprint of a posted document;
  • the life cycle shared by all statutory filings — compute, export, mark submitted, amend — and the filed vs computed comparison screens;
  • a statement account mapping for charts that do not use the standard account codes.

It depends only on Odoo's account and mail, so it works on Community and Enterprise.

Settings

Accounting → Configuration → Settings, block Czech / Slovak Localization:

Setting What it does
Extra accounting menus (Community) Installs OCA account_usability, which adds the accounting menus Enterprise has (general ledger, journals, aged balances…). Shown on Community only.
Financial reports (Community) Installs OCA account_financial_report: general ledger, trial balance, partner ledger, aged balance, journal ledger. Shown on Community only.
Default tax authority The tax office (daňový úrad / finanční úřad) your filings are addressed to. Only offices of the company's fiscal country are offered.
VAT declared in a later period An account for VAT deferral entries — see VAT deferral. Empty: off.
Year-end closing journals The journals holding the year-end closing and reopening entries (e.g. UZAVIERKA, OTVORENIE). Their entries are left out of the financial statements, the income-tax return and the financial reports, so that closing the year does not wipe out the balance sheet and the profit and loss. Leave empty if the year is never closed in this database.

The full suites add their own switches to this block, one per optional module.

Your company

On the company form (Settings → Companies), after Country:

  • Tax Authority — the same field as Default tax authority above.
  • Entity Type — legal entity or natural person, from the entity types of the company's country; some forms change with it.

The commercial-register entry (Spoločnosť zapísaná v obchodnom registri… / zapsaná v obchodním rejstříku…) goes in Odoo's own Trade Registry field on the company, which the Slovak and Czech localizations print on the invoice. This module used to offer a separate Registration Info field that no document printed; it is gone from the form, and upgrading copies a value entered there into Trade Registry if that was empty.

Contacts and the IČO

On contacts whose country is the Czech Republic or Slovakia:

  • The company registry field is labelled IČO, and it is shown on individuals too (Odoo normally shows it only on companies), because a sole trader buying online is created as a person and still has an IČO.
  • The IČO is checked when you save: it must have 6 to 8 digits and a valid check digit (the weighted modulo-11 used by both countries). A wrong value is refused with a message naming the company — typing the company name, the VAT number or Test into the field is no longer possible.
  • A valid IČO is stored with leading zeros to eight digits: 580007 becomes 00580007.
  • Entity Type appears before the VAT number, for classifying the partner in statutory forms.

Contacts of other countries are not checked: a German HRB 12345 is accepted as it is.

Tax offices and entity types

Accounting → Configuration → CZ/SK Localization:

  • Tax Authorities — the offices filings are addressed to, each with a stable code, the code written into the XML (Submission Code) and, for a Czech territorial workplace (územní pracoviště), the regional office it belongs to. The Czech and Slovak statutory modules load the offices; you normally only pick one. The offices listed are those of the fiscal countries of the companies currently selected in the company switcher: working in a Czech and a Slovak company at once, you see both.
  • Person / Entity Types — legal entity, natural person and similar categories per country, loaded the same way.
  • Statement account mapping — see below. Visible to accounting administrators.

VAT period of a document

Taxable supply date

The customer invoice and bill lists get a Taxable Supply Date column (optional, shown by default), and the search gets a filter and a grouping by it. The taxable supply date (deň dodania / DUZP) decides the VAT period of a sale.

VAT period declared

On invoices, credit notes and bills, after the due date, VAT period declared names the period in which the VAT is reported when that differs from the usual date. Leave it empty in the normal case.

The statutory returns choose the period of each document like this:

Document Period
Customer invoice, customer credit note VAT period declared if filled; otherwise the taxable supply date; otherwise the accounting date
Vendor bill, refund, any other entry VAT period declared if filled; otherwise the accounting date

Fill it on a bill whose deduction you claim later than the period it is booked in, on a correction declared in a later period, or on a document entered late. The legal background is in Legal background.

VAT deferral entries

When VAT period declared falls in a later month than the accounting date, the VAT return reports the tax later, but account 343 still carries it in the month of booking, so 343 no longer agrees with the return. If you set an account in VAT declared in a later period, posting such a document also creates two journal entries in the first miscellaneous journal:

  1. on the accounting date, the tax is moved from the VAT account to the deferral account;
  2. on the declared date, it is moved back. If that date is still ahead, the entry is posted automatically when it comes.

Only tax lines that take part in the tax closing are moved. The entries carry no taxes or tax tags, so no return reads them. The document shows VAT deferral: n entries with a link to them; each entry shows the document under VAT Deferral Of. Resetting the document to draft, cancelling it, or changing the declared date cancels the entries (and creates new ones where still needed).

Legal background

The VAT period declared exists because the deduction may be claimed later than the supply:

  • Czech Republic — the deduction may be claimed at the earliest for the period in which its conditions (above all, holding the tax document) are met, and no later than the end of the second calendar year after the year the right arose: § 73 odst. 2 and 3 of the VAT Act No. 235/2004 Sb..
  • Slovakia — the deduction is made at the earliest in the period the right arose and at the latest in the last period of that calendar year, provided the payer holds the invoice by the deadline for that return; otherwise in the period the invoice arrives: § 51 ods. 2 of the VAT Act No. 222/2004 Z. z..

The module records the period you choose. It does not check that the choice respects these limits.

Statutory footprint

A posted invoice or journal entry has a Statutory footprint button (accounting users only). It lists the statutory report rows the document feeds — form, row code and description — and, where a filing for the period already exists, the filing with a link to it. An empty Filing column means no return for that period has been generated yet; the rows are what it would feed. Which forms appear depends on the statutory modules installed.

Statutory filings: the common life cycle

The VAT return, control statement, EC sales list and the other forms are separate modules, but they share one life cycle provided here:

Step Button What happens
Draft → Preview Compute the rows are computed from the ledger
Preview → Exported Export XML content checks run, the XML is produced and validated against the official schema, and attached. A failed check blocks the export; a warning does not, but it is shown in a notification, posted to the chatter and kept in Export warnings until the next export — read it before filing
Exported → Submitted Mark Submitted the exported XML is frozen as the filed copy (Filed XML), the date is recorded and the filing is locked: it can no longer be recomputed, re-exported or deleted
File it opens a delivery record for the authority's receipts — see l10n_cssk_submission_base
Submitted → Draft Reset to Draft accounting administrators only; the filed copy is kept
Dodatočný / opravný on a submitted filing: creates a draft amendment linked to the original

Every XML ever marked submitted stays in Filed history, so after a reset, recompute and resubmit the originally filed copy is still there. Enter the confirmation number from the portal in Submission reference.

Historical filings. A filing migrated from a previous system is in state Historical filing: it records what was actually filed and cannot be computed, exported or submitted. It can be amended, and it can be compared with what Odoo computes for its period (Compare with computed, see below).

Filed vs computed

Accounting → Reporting → Statutory Reports → Filed vs computed:

  • Comparisons — one line per filing and per basis of comparison, with the counts of rows that agree, findings, rows still to review, and the totals.
  • Rows to review — the individual rows across all comparisons, filtered to those needing an answer.

A comparison is created by a button on a filing. Compare with computed on a historical filing puts it beside what Odoo computes for the same period; the Slovak suite adds comparisons of one filing with another and with account 343 (see l10n_sk_datadance). Compared against says which of these the right-hand column holds:

Compared against Right-hand column
The filing, recomputed what Odoo computes for the filing's period
The ledger the balance in the accounts, e.g. 343
Another filing a different filing for the same period

Each row has a result:

Result Meaning
Agrees same figure on both sides
Amount differs same row, different amount
Same amount, different row the two sides put the same amount on different rows (shown as a linked pair)
Only the filing has it / Only we compute it the row exists on one side only
Vocabularies not mapped the two sides use row codes that cannot be matched
Difference is expected a structural gap, e.g. the control statement covers less than the return
Informational, not a control shown for information, never a finding

Work through the findings by setting a row's status — Asked the accountant, Filing was right, Filing was wrong, We are wrong, Understood, no action — and writing what the accountant said in Note. The answer and the note survive a re-run: re-running updates the figures only. A row that no longer appears on either side is kept and marked No longer compared rather than deleted.

The comparison's own state follows its rows — Everything agrees, To review, Being worked through, Every difference answered — and cannot be set by hand. When you have reviewed the whole comparison, click Sign off; Withdraw sign-off removes it. A re-run does not remove a sign-off.

Statement account mapping

The statutory statements read balances by account code, using the codes of the standard chart of accounts. A chart taken over from another system often uses its own analytical codes — 461001 for a long-term bank loan where the Slovak balance sheet expects 461100 — and such an account lands on no row.

Accounting → Configuration → CZ/SK Localization → Statement account mapping (accounting administrators) lets you keep your chart and say under which code an account is reported:

Field Meaning
Account your account
Balance side Any balance, or Debit balance only / Credit balance only — e.g. a bank account reported as a short-term bank loan only when it is overdrawn
Reported code the code the statement reads it as, e.g. 461200; a plain code, no spaces or operators

A side-dependent mapping applies only to balance-sheet (as-of) balances; in the profit and loss the account keeps its own code. An account can have either one Any balance mapping or debit and/or credit mappings, not both. The mapping applies to the preview, the XML and the drill-down alike.

Limitations

  • The IČO check proves the number is well formed, not that it exists; checking against the register is done by other modules.
  • VAT period declared is not checked against the statutory time limits.
  • VAT deferral entries go to the first miscellaneous journal of the company; the journal cannot be chosen. A company with none gets an error on posting.
  • Export warnings are shown on the filing's chatter and in the export notification; the filing forms do not yet show them as a banner.

Legislation referenced on this page

  • Zákon č. 235/2004 Sb., o dani z přidané hodnoty
  • Zákon č. 222/2004 Z. z. o dani z pridanej hodnoty
